title: U.S. House · New York's 20th Congressional District
area: Capital Region, covering Albany, Schenectady, and Amsterdam and surrounding areas.

context.text: Both parties' primaries were canceled: incumbent Paul Tonko advanced unopposed on the Democratic and Working Families Party lines, and Ralph Ambrosio advanced unopposed on the Republican and Conservative Party lines. As of September 22, 2026, Cook Political Report and Inside Elections rated the general election "Solid Democratic" and Decision Desk and Sabato's Crystal Ball rated it "Safe Democratic."

positions.summary: Official issues page says he will continue to support policies that strengthen the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will continue to support policies that strengthen the ACA and improve health care for every American.

positions.summary: Official issues page says Congress must act on gun reform and lists proposals including an assault weapons ban and a three-day waiting period for handgun purchases.
positions.quote: we cannot leave it to them alone to fight for commonsense gun reform.

positions.summary: His 2019 climate framework, still posted on his official site, calls for science-based targets for greenhouse gas neutrality by mid-century and accelerating the clean energy transition.
positions.quote: Adopt Science-Based Targets for Greenhouse Gas Neutrality by Mid-Century

record.text: Serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee (Oversight and Investigations; Energy; Environment subcommittees) and the House Budget Committee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Chaired the House Energy and Commerce Committee's Environment and Climate Change Subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

priorities.text: Says his campaign centers on lowering the cost of living through tax cuts and deregulation, and on expanding domestic energy production to reduce energy costs.
priorities.quote: We have to tackle crushing costs and lack of opportunity through tax cutting and deregulation.

priorities.text: Says he would prioritize public safety and border security, and supports term limits, voter ID, and parental rights in education.
priorities.quote: Restore Public Safety & Secure Our Borders Permanently

positions.summary: In a 2026 Protect the Adirondacks questionnaire, he opposed the Polluters Pay Climate Fund Act, said restrictions on fossil fuels and nuclear while subsidizing other energy sources have raised energy costs, and said fracking bans harm New York.
positions.quote: Restrictions on fossil fuel and nuclear while subsidizing non-scalable and inefficient energy sources has driven up energy costs and stifled economic prosperity.

positions.summary: In a Feb. 4, 2026 campaign press release, said local law enforcement should coordinate with federal authorities to deport people in the country illegally who have committed crimes, and said abolishing ICE would make communities less safe.
positions.quote: If Albany Democrats were serious about protecting public safety, they would let local law enforcement coordinate with federal authorities to deport criminal illegal aliens.

statements.quote: America’s healthcare crisis is not the result of free-market failure; it is the direct consequence of federal distortions that have systematically destroyed price transparency and consumer choice.
statements.context: In his campaign healthcare policy brief

statements.quote: Paul Tonko’s vote against Israeli aid is more than just a policy disagreement; it is a failure of moral clarity
statements.context: In a July 16, 2026 campaign press release criticizing Rep. Tonko's vote against the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act

researchNotes: Ambrosio's campaign website (ambrosioforcongress.com) was reachable on this pass and supplied biography and priorities above; he still has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his Ballotpedia page has no independent biography section. A fact-check removed a `guns` position drawn from a generic "defending the right to self-defense" line in his public-safety priorities list, since his issues page never mentions guns, firearms, or the Second Amendment and does not squarely address gun-law policy, so no gun position is recorded. Pass 2 (Oct. 2026): his campaign press room supplied immigration-enforcement and Israel-aid positions and a healthcare statement. Tonko has not stated specific 2026 campaign priorities on his Ballotpedia page; his entry here relies on biography and committee assignments. Ambrosio's Israel-aid remarks criticize his opponent's vote and do not themselves state support for continuing aid, so they are recorded as a statement.
